finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 data is passed to Marshal.load, enabling arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains (e.g., Gem::Requirement/Gem::Installer/ERB-based universal gadgets).
finding.source: POST /restore form parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication required

trace.note: POST /restore route, no auth before_filter or any middleware
params[:state] Base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
state.inspect is invoked on the deserialized object, which also triggers gadgets that fire on inspect/to_s/hash/==, but the load itself is already sufficient for gadget execution

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no HMAC/signature on the blob, no class allowlist, no use of safe formats (JSON). Sinatra's Rack::Protection does not protect against this (CSRF protection does not apply to non-browser clients). The file is the entire app; no before filters or middleware are defined. A nil params[:state] would just raise (500) and is not a guard.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-7 matches the trace: the unauthenticated POST /restore passes Base64-decoded params[:state] straight into Marshal.load at app.rb:6, and no auth, signature, allowlist or middleware exists anywhere (app.rb is the only file).

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64-decoded attacker-controlled params[:state] straight to Marshal.load in the POST /restore route (app.rb:5), with no auth, signature, or class allowlist anywhere in the single-file app, and app.rb:7 calls inspect on the result.
